 THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ADITYA KUMAR  MOHAPATRA  ORDER 11.11.2024 Order No.
02. 1.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. Heard Senior learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned Counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the Informant.
Perused the records.

3. This is an application under Section 438, Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioner for anticipatory bail,
involving offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 120-B, 34 of I.P.C. and Sections 66(C), 66(D) of I.T. Act in C.T. Case No.399 of 2024 of the Court of learned S.D.J.M.,
Bhubaneswar arising out of Cyber Crime P.S. Case No.11 of 2024.
4.

sentences.text: It is stated by learned Senior counsel for the Petitioner that due to misunderstanding the present F.I.R. has been registered against the Petitioner at the instance of the informant.
He further contended in the meantime the alleged money has already been repaid to the informant by the Petitioner.
He further submitted that the Petitioner does not have any criminal antecedent.

He further contended that a sum of Rs.12,80,000/- by D.D. No.722341 drawn on State Bank of India,
Parmial Chowk, Waghawadi Road Branch, Bhavanagar, Gujrat has been handed over to the Jaydevsinh Ashoksinh Jadeja vs State Of Odisha .....

1 informant.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the Informant submitted that the informant has already received the money and the demand draft has already been encashed.
In such view of the matter, learned counsel for the Informant submitted that he has no subsisting grievance, as such he does not want to oppose the bail application of the present Petitioner.

6. Learned counsel for the State submitted that although the amount has already been paid,
however, the Petitioner be released on pre-arrest bail on such terms and conditions in the event this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on pre-arrest bail.

7. Considering the submissions made by learned counsels appearing for the parties, on a careful examination of the materials on record, further taking note of the submission of learned counsel for the Informant that the Informant has already been received a sum of Rs.12,80,000/-, although I am not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner, however it is observed that, in the event the Petitioner surrenders and moves for bail before the learned court in seisin over the matter within a period of three weeks from today, he shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as the learned Magistrate may deem just and proper.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of the bail.
8. The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.
9. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge Anil Location: High Court of Orissa Jaydevsinh Ashoksinh Jadeja vs State Of Odisha .....
